Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

could you make a family dinner calendar for april 2027, and address it to Ellis, not Leonie. i mean Ellis is the person who should receive the calendar; Leonie is still one of the people eating the meals, just not who the request is for. the household is Ellis, Leonie, Mara and Owen, and Peter and June are Ellis and Leonie's grandparents. Please cover dinner only, not breakfast or lunch, and put something against every date from april 1 through april 30 so we can look ahead without filling in gaps ourselves. It should be a usable plan for this particular household, not a general collection of dinner ideas, and the dates should line up with the actual weekdays in April 2027.

We are trying to keep weekday evenings manageable. Most dinners should be realistic to cook at home without a long project, and a short preparation note would help when the meal needs a bit of advance work. Don't turn the plan into full recipes, though. Put the date, meal, and any useful timing or attendance note where they can be scanned together. On Mondays make the dinner vegetarian. Leonie doesn't like mushrooms, so please don't make mushrooms a main ingredient or build a meal around them. Ellis has a peanut allergy; avoid peanuts and peanut oil, rather than just suggesting that someone leave them off their own serving. The rest of the household eats meat and fish, and we'd like a mix across the month instead of chicken showing up almost every night.

There are some particular schedule things to catch. Ellis is at evening soccer practice on Wednesday April 7 and gets home late, so that dinner needs to be something that can wait or be set aside easily. Mara works late on Tuesday April 13, so don't plan a meal that depends on her being home to start it. On Thursday April 15 Owen has a meeting and the family will eat after 7; something that reheats well or can finish later is better than a meal that needs to be served right away. Ellis has an evening school event on Tuesday April 20, and a portion should be kept for Ellis to eat later. Leonie is away on a choir trip Sunday April 11, so plan that dinner for the other three household members, not as if the whole family is there. These are only the listed evenings, don't infer that anyone is away on other dates.

Sunday April 4 is different because Peter and June are coming to the house for dinner, making six people at the table. Please allow for that larger meal in the amount and choose something suitable for a relaxed family visit; no need to make it a formal occasion. On Sunday April 18, the four household members are eating dinner at Peter and June's home, so mark the calendar as away from home instead of assigning a home-cooked menu for that date. Owen said, “If it's on the calendar, I can shop for it on Sunday.” We normally do the main grocery shop on Sundays, and a short grocery list grouped by week would make the plan more useful. Keep it tied to the meals in the calendar and call out anything needed from the pantry only if it matters for that week's cooking.

1) Food and weeknight details: There is rice, pasta, red lentils, canned tomatoes and frozen peas in the pantry already. There is also chicken stock, but it isn't vegetarian, so don't use it in the Monday meals. We don't need quantities for every pantry ingredient; just avoid making the shopping list tell us to buy the items already here unless a meal uses more than the amount on hand, which isn't specified. Friday evenings are deliberately flexible because the family sometimes decides together at the end of the week. Mark each Friday as flexible rather than choosing a fixed dinner or assuming a particular restaurant. Saturdays can use leftovers or a simple meal, but don't label every Saturday as leftovers automatically. We would still like a clear entry for each Saturday.

Please keep the meal choices varied and ordinary enough for a family table. A recipe may use a few ingredients that aren't listed in the pantry, but don't make the whole month depend on specialty products. Avoid repeating the same dinner in the same week. Include the Sunday April 25 shopping day in the right week when you group the grocery list, and don't put meals from early May into this April calendar. If a meal can provide useful leftovers for another evening, note that briefly, but don't make leftovers an extra required meal on a different date unless you actually list it there. The short prep notes can mention setting something out earlier or saving a portion; no need for cooking instructions step by step.

The calendar can be a simple table or another clear date-by-date layout, with weekdays visible so the soccer, work and evening-event notes are easy to find. Put the weekly grocery lists after the calendar rather than mixing shopping items into the meal names. Keep the calendar readable on a printed page, but it does not need decoration or a nutrition analysis. The kitchen has one oven and two burners, and there is no slow cooker, so don't schedule several oven dishes that need the oven at the same time or rely on a slow cooker. Please use that equipment information when choosing meals; it is separate from the meal-preference notes and should not get lost at the end.", "output": "Create a family dinner calendar for April 2027 and address it to Ellis, not Leonie.
